lines.raw: The idea in one sentence.
lines.say: The idea in one sentence.

lines.raw: Building an episode means finding the **trigger** claim, pulling every claim for that member in the **window**, keeping only the ones the **relatedness rules** say belong, and adding up their cost.
lines.say: Building an episode means finding the trigger claim, pulling every claim for that member in the window, keeping only the ones the relatedness rules say belong, and adding up their cost.

lines.raw: The US version: the build steps.
lines.say: The U S version: the build steps.

scenes.section: The US version: the build steps

lines.raw: Step 1: Find triggers.
lines.say: Step 1: Find triggers.

lines.raw: Group hospital stays (DRGs) and outpatient claims, then select those that match the trigger rule.
lines.say: Group hospital stays (D R G's) and outpatient claims, then select those that match the trigger rule.

lines.raw: Step 2: Check the clean period and eligibility.
lines.say: Step 2: Check the clean period and eligibility.

lines.raw: Start a new episode only if no episode of the same type is open.
lines.say: Start a new episode only if no episode of the same type is open.

lines.raw: Check the member was enrolled for the whole window, or the episode will look cheap because care is missing.
lines.say: Check the member was enrolled for the whole window, or the episode will look cheap because care is missing.

lines.raw: Step 3: Set the window.
lines.say: Step 3: Set the window.

lines.raw: Work out the start and end dates from the trigger dates.
lines.say: Work out the start and end dates from the trigger dates.

lines.raw: Step 4: Pull candidate claims.
lines.say: Step 4: Pull candidate claims.

lines.raw: All medical (and, if in scope, pharmacy) claims for that member with service dates in the window.
lines.say: All medical (and, if in scope, pharmacy) claims for that member with service dates in the window.

lines.raw: Step 5: Apply relatedness rules.
lines.say: Step 5: Apply relatedness rules.

lines.raw: Keep claims whose diagnoses or procedures are on the episode's lists, or keep everything for an all-cause episode.
lines.say: Keep claims whose diagnoses or procedures are on the episode's lists, or keep everything for an all-cause episode.

lines.raw: Step 6: Assign each claim once.
lines.say: Step 6: Assign each claim once.

lines.raw: If a claim could belong to two episodes, follow priority rules so it is counted only once.
lines.say: If a claim could belong to two episodes, follow priority rules so it is counted only once.

lines.raw: Step 7: Sum and compare.
lines.say: Step 7: Sum and compare.

lines.raw: Add the allowed amounts, then compare with the expected cost for a similar patient.
lines.say: Add the allowed amounts, then compare with the expected cost for a similar patient.

lines.raw: Why the follow-up visit is $0.
lines.say: Why the follow-up visit is 0 dollars.

lines.raw: For a major operation, the surgeon's fee already covers routine follow-up visits for 90 days (the **global surgery period**).

lines.raw: Robert's episode cost.
lines.say: Robert's episode cost.

lines.raw: Before (pre-trigger). Claims: Surgeon visit, pre-surgery tests. Allowed: $180 + $150 = **$330**.
lines.say: Before (pre-trigger). Claims: Surgeon visit, pre-surgery tests. Allowed: 180 dollars and 150 dollars = 330 dollars.

lines.raw: Trigger. Claims: Hospital stay, surgeon, anaesthesia. Allowed: $14,500 + $1,600 + $500 = **$16,600**.
lines.say: Trigger. Claims: Hospital stay, surgeon, anaesthesia. Allowed: 14500 dollars and 1600 dollars and 500 dollars = 16600 dollars.

lines.raw: After (post-trigger). Claims: Pharmacy, physiotherapy, follow-up, ER visit. Allowed: $60 + $1,800 + $0 + $1,200 = **$3,060**.
lines.say: After (post-trigger). Claims: Pharmacy, physiotherapy, follow-up, E R visit. Allowed: 60 dollars and 1800 dollars and 0 dollars and 1200 dollars = 3060 dollars.

lines.raw: **Episode total (related care)**. Claims: 9 claims. Allowed: **$19,990**.
lines.say: Episode total (related care). Claims: 9 claims. Allowed: 19990 dollars.

lines.raw: All-cause version (adds the diabetes check). Claims: 10 claims. Allowed: $20,130.
lines.say: All-cause version (adds the diabetes check). Claims: 10 claims. Allowed: 20130 dollars.

lines.raw: What a similar episode is expected to cost, from a model that uses age, conditions and other risk factors.

lines.raw: Robert's diabetes raises his expected cost.

lines.raw: O/E ratio (observed ÷ expected).
lines.say: O/E ratio (observed ÷ expected).

lines.raw: Actual cost divided by expected.
lines.say: Actual cost divided by expected.

lines.raw: Below 1.0 = cheaper than expected.
lines.say: Below 1.0 = cheaper than expected.

lines.raw: Price standardization.
lines.say: Price standardization.

lines.raw: Replacing each claim's actual price with a standard price for that service, so a hospital in an expensive city is not penalised for local prices.
lines.say: Replacing each claim's actual price with a standard price for that service, so a hospital in an expensive city is not penalised for local prices.

lines.raw: What is left is differences in **what care was used**.
lines.say: What is left is differences in what care was used.

lines.raw: Outlier cap.
lines.say: Outlier cap.

lines.raw: Limiting extreme episodes (for example at a high percentile) so a handful of very rare cases do not dominate averages.
lines.say: Limiting extreme episodes (for example at a high percentile) so a handful of very rare cases do not dominate averages.

lines.raw: Robert's O/E ratio.
lines.say: Robert's O/E ratio.

lines.raw: O/E equals $19,990 ÷ $21,000 expected equals 0.95.
lines.say: O/E equals 19990 dollars ÷ 21000 dollars expected equals 0.95.

lines.raw: For example: Robert's episode cost about 5% less than expected for a patient like him, even with an ER visit after surgery.
lines.say: For example: Robert's episode cost about 5 percent less than expected for a patient like him, even with an E R visit after surgery.
